Gun License NYC · Homepage · Section 4

TheCount V14 — catch, replace, clear

The loop is now the product. Satisfied documents pass and the reticle moves on. A flagged one keeps its stamp, then gets taken off the desk and replaced — and when the reticle comes back around, the replacement clears, and its ledger row turns green. Resolving one problem raises a new flag elsewhere, so the desk never settles into all-green. Verdicts now hold for about 1.6 seconds and fade rather than blinking off — the head is already two cells away before the stamp goes. The frames below are live.

What changed, and why

The stamp had 430msThe verdict landed at 820ms into a 1250ms stop and was wiped the instant the head moved on — and its own entrance animation only finished at ~440ms, so it was being erased as it arrived. It now lands after the scan completes, holds past the head’s departure, and fades over half a second. 430ms → 1600ms of visible verdict.
Why it blinked instead of fadingThe entrance animations were the visible state, so removing data-stage snapped the wash, glyph and label back to scale(0) — no opacity transition can fade something already collapsed. The fix is to base those elements in their final transforms and let opacity alone do the showing and hiding; the animations then only add the flourish.
The bug you spottedThe entrance deal animation was still attached to the wall — data-play never got removed. The eight sheets with the idle breath carry a :not([data-audit]) guard, so the instant a reticle landed on one, the guard failed, the deal rule won the cascade back, and the sheet re-flew in from the pile. Dropping data-play when the entrance ends fixes it.
The loop is now the productScan → flag → we get it replaced → rescan → clear. Satisfied documents pass and the head moves on; flagged ones keep their stamp, settled to about half strength, until the sheet is lifted away and a fresh one drops in and draws itself. That is the service, animated — not a status board re-confirming itself.
The empty slot is held openA dashed hairline stays in the cell while the swap happens, so a replacement never reads the way the bug did — as a document simply vanishing. The outgoing sheet lifts above its neighbours on the way out.
The desk never goes all-greenClearing a replacement raises a new flag a few seconds later, on whichever satisfied sheet is furthest from the reticle — so you catch it in the corner of your eye. The bucket is chosen by whichever is furthest below target, which pins the mix near 17 / 3 / 3 / 1 while still letting the numbers breathe.
Back to one reticleYou noticed there were two. With this much choreography a second head competing for attention makes the story unreadable — you need to be able to follow one document from flag to replacement to clearance. The step is faster to compensate: about 30 seconds a lap.
The ledger resolves with itRow 11 is the 18-hour safety course — the expired one, and the same certificate the ProductFeature card warns is aging out. Watch its dot go red → replaced → green as the loop runs. The right column is no longer inert.
